original_test_intent: Verify BMC GPU inventory behavior across distinct power domains: GPU details remain correctly available with host off while management/auxiliary power is present, then become absent or deasserted after the specified AC loss and remain in the approved state after AC restore to standby, exactly as the platform design defines.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify SUT/BMC/GPU population by UUID/serial/slot/BDF/firmware and authoritative GUI/Redfish resources; capture host-on baseline; quiesce and perform approved host soft-off; after readiness capture complete GUI and Redfish inventory; qualified operator removes all defined AC feeds for the required dwell and documents GPU rail deassertion; collect any still-available management evidence; restore AC without booting host and wait for standby readiness; capture GUI/Redfish again; compare every field to the engineer-approved state matrix and restore the final power state.
manual_activity: An authorized operator quiesces the host, controls the approved host-off and all-feed AC transitions, captures WebUI evidence and owns console/power recovery; the agent collects Redfish and correlated logs.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC firmware and GPU UUID/serial/slot/BDF/model/firmware configuration
Canonical Redfish GPU inventory resources/fields and matching WebUI locations
Power-domain definition for host off, GPU deassert, complete AC removal and AC-restored standby
Per-state expected presence/absence, field freshness, cache invalidation and readiness timeouts
PSU/feed/PDU map, maintenance approval, workload drain, final state and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Quiesce active workloads and data before host or AC power changes
Name every AC feed/outlet and prove complete removal for deassertion; never guess PDU targets
Record BMC and host power state plus timestamp with every inventory sample
Distinguish live GPU data from cached inventory using vendor freshness/status semantics
Stop on wrong target, BMC loss, unexpected boot, stale/partial inventory, GPU fault or failure to reach standby; no automatic cycle retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, power/state matrix, inventory endpoints, approval and recovery
Collect secret-safe Redfish JSON, power status, BMC/SEL and host evidence at each approved checkpoint
Coordinate only named approved power control after separate execution confirmation; GUI and physical transitions remain operator-owned
Do not infer expected presence, issue generic power commands, clear logs, repeat AC cycling or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the four-state power-domain and GPU-inventory/freshness matrix
Approve feed/outlet topology, timing, final state and safe recovery
Review GUI/Redfish/power evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and first criterion require GPU details while host is off, while criterion 2 says previously displayed details disappear `after AC` without specifying whether that means during complete AC loss or after AC is restored to standby. The expected final inventory state is therefore ambiguous across the stated sequence.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The power-domain inventory purpose is clear. Engineering can supply the exact per-state presence/freshness matrix and timing; static review completes while disruptive execution remains gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2220 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00003-V002: approve the SUT/BMC/GPU UUID/serial/slot/BDF/model/firmware configuration, canonical Redfish resources and WebUI fields, exact host-on/host-off/complete-AC-deassert/AC-restored-standby power domains and PSU/feed/PDU map, per-state GPU-detail presence/absence/cache-freshness/readiness timing—especially the meaning of `no longer present after AC`—plus workload drain, final state, stop conditions and console/power recovery.

review_improvement: Makes the ambiguous `after AC` expectation explicit, prevents stale inventory from passing and converts disruptive power actions into a traceable GUI/Redfish state matrix with recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Host soft-off can leave auxiliary rails and BMC-visible GPU inventory intact, whereas complete AC loss can remove both GPU power and portions of management reachability. After AC restore to standby, BMC may repopulate inventory from cache or discover devices only after host boot. Therefore presence/absence has no universal answer; the platform state matrix and freshness semantics are the acceptance oracle. Each sample must be tied to actual power-domain evidence, or a stale WebUI/Redfish record could falsely satisfy either criterion.
